measuredBy: Onboarding funnel (steps 1 to 10 in Telemetry) and the timing in scripts/probes/ftue.py
failureMeaning: Players bounce before the game starts. First-play bounce is a top negative ranking signal.
label: Documented signal (bounce under 60 s and 61 to 180 s); the 15 s number is a creator target

measuredBy: Onboarding funnel step for the first reward, plus the FTUE probe
failureMeaning: The core loop does not pay off fast enough to hold a new player.
source: research/video-notes/tizzy-3-viral-games.md section 1 (first ~90 seconds); research/ui-motion-audit.md (reference games showed a first reward at about 1:20 and 3:00)
label: Creator claim plus Observed in two reference games

target: At least 80% of new players launch their first mission within 30 s of the first prompt
measuredBy: Closed test with 20 to 30 players, plus the funnel step timestamps
failureMeaning: The first-session flow is unclear. Iterate the Advisor steps before adding features.
source: research/concepts.md (closed-test thresholds, adapted from the archived concept to this game)
label: Team target

target: A second reason to keep playing is on screen before 3 minutes
measuredBy: Funnel step after the first reward, and the kid-tester report
failureMeaning: Players finish one loop and leave in the 61 to 180 s bounce window.
label: Documented window (bounce segments); the target is a team target

target: At least 10 min on average; design sessions of 20 to 40 min with a reason to return
failureMeaning: Playtime is the second main return signal. Playtime beyond 60 min per player per day earns no extra credit.
source: research/video-notes/rasdev-algorithm.md section 5; research/sources.md (Creator Hub Discovery, 60 min cap)
label: Documented (60 min cap); the 10 and 20 to 40 min figures are creator claims

target: 12 to 15% (stretch 16%); in a closed test, at least 25% return within 48 h
measuredBy: Creator Analytics D1 retention; closed-test return rate before launch
failureMeaning: The first session does not create a reason to come back. Organic Home players decide ranking.
source: research/video-notes/tizzy-3-viral-games.md (D1 about 6 to 8% rising to about 16% after a progression overhaul); research/concepts.md (25% within 48 h proxy)
label: Creator claim, Unverified

target: 2 to 3% as a first working target
measuredBy: Creator Analytics D2 to 7 retention window
failureMeaning: Progression, offline growth and daily rewards are not pulling players back across a week.
source: research/video-notes/rasdev-algorithm.md section 1 (D1, D2 to 7 and D8 to 28 windows are Documented; weights are not published). No published number was found in the research.
label: Team target; replace with the Creator Analytics baseline after launch

measuredBy: Votes from the games API (Market page, Games live numbers)
failureMeaning: Players who try it do not rate it well, which hurts recommendations.
source: research/market-snapshot.md section 2 (16 reference games all sit between 85% and 97% like ratio, observed 2026-10-17)
label: Observed (API) for the reference range; the 80% floor is a team target

target: Test at least 3 icon and thumbnail variants and keep the best; no public number exists
measuredBy: Creator Analytics impressions to plays, per icon and thumbnail variant
failureMeaning: Players judge the icon and name only. A weak one stops Roblox expanding the game past a small Home audience.
label: Documented signal (PTR is a top-tier signal); no number is published

target: About 2% of players as a planning assumption
measuredBy: Payers divided by players in Creator Analytics
failureMeaning: Revenue plans built on the assumption are too high. Plan from cohort data instead.
source: research/monetization-tactics.md (2 to 3% payer conversion for simulator-type games, profitable.app; stated there as assumptions, not data)
label: Unverified (third-party model)

target: No fixed target until D7 cohort data exists; plan from cohort ARPDAU times realistic DAU with decay
measuredBy: Creator Analytics revenue per daily active user, by cohort
failureMeaning: Planning from a weekend peak overstates revenue and hides the decay curve.
source: research/video-notes/takeaways.md constraint 13; research/video-notes/tizzy-3-viral-games.md (ARPDAU about 0.9 to 1.0 rising to about 2.0, units not stated)
label: Creator claim (units unstated)

target: No script errors on the first-session path; under 1% of sessions with any client error
measuredBy: ScriptContext.Error counts by script name (server) and Telemetry.Client error counts, plus the playtester console check
failureMeaning: Players hit broken screens or lose progress. Fix before any promotion.
label: Team target

target: 60 FPS on a mid PC, 30+ FPS on a low-end phone, under 600 MB on mobile
measuredBy: MicroProfiler and the Developer Console on a phone each milestone
failureMeaning: Low-end phones stutter or crash, and the phone layout loses most of its audience.
label: Team target
